topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and introduces the learning objectives for this final session on cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional treatment modalities—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated toxicities and resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor-specific biological vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic defects of cancer cells, such as hormone dependency, checkpoint loss, oncolytic virus susceptibility, and synthetic lethality from DNA repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the rationale of targeting hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and detail the cellular mechanisms through which tumors develop resistance and drug addiction.

topics.label: Therapeutic monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how engineered monoclonal antibodies are utilized to disrupt oncogenic surface signaling or selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads to cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and cellular immune treatments
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the interaction between tumors and the immune system alongside immunotherapeutic interventions, including immune checkpoint blockade, BiTEs, and CAR T-cell therapy.

topics.label: Overarching challenges, historical progress, and future directions in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize the broader clinical challenges, historical survival trends, early detection strategies, and ethical dilemmas shaping the future of cancer treatment.
